attackOnCentralClaim:
The claim: make the artifact auditable — spend climx's real machinery on three routes, make «no claim without evidence» a non-optional field so M1 is a compile-time property, and put a /colofon on the page so a reader opening the repo finds its claims about itself already checkable.

IT LARGELY SURVIVES, and I want to be precise about why, because this is the most first-hand-verifiable candidate text I could check. Nearly every checkable number in it checked out: `fallback` really is non-optional in the router signature; `base: '/portfolio/'` really is in vite.config.ts; the two tsconfigs are byte-IDENTICAL (stronger than its own hedged 'differ only in comments'); portfolio's main.tsx really has no restore block; portfolio's reset.css really is missing .skip-link, the button base, `input,button,textarea,select{font:inherit}` and button:focus-visible while keeping a:focus-visible, and .page really is 44rem vs climx's 64rem; PrimitivesLab really has no CSS module; every contrast figure is right to 2 dp; and every MEASUREMENTS.md row it cites exists at the date cited — 9,852 records -> 2,463 files (L14, 2026-07-28), 44,266 B gzip (L15), 66.66 KB gzip (L30), 463 B gz (L73), 51/51 tests + cobertura lib 98.92% (L75-77) — as does the reason for excluding Lighthouse (L45/51-52 record it against project-tw, the pre-rename URL). The README/MEASUREMENTS 41-vs-51 inconsistency it flags is real (climx README L32 says 41). It even correctly caught that index.html is lang="en".

WHERE IT EMBARRASSES ITSELF: the objective's named workload is a recruiter deciding in ~20 seconds on `/`, arriving from a GitHub profile or CV link. That reader never opens the repo, never reaches /colofon, and never observes that `evidence` is non-optional. So the headline over-reaches its own instrument: M1 is measured by hand enumeration of the rendered DOM, which the type system does not perform — the compile-time property raises the AUTHORING floor, not the MEASURED score. The candidate concedes exactly this in weakestPoint; the thesis line does not. Second: the implicit competitor — 'an editorial promise' / 'a hand-rolled switch' — is a partial strawman, because the objective itself already admits a single-route design as legitimate (with the burden of reaching M6>=4 by other means), and the candidate never engages that admissible competitor on the quality of `/`, only on route count. On its own admission ~3 of 17 files serve the scored reader.

WHERE IT WINS: the reader who does open the repo, and — more importantly — the A2/ATF gate itself. Repo-ROOT-only links cut the quality veto to 6 hand-checkable URLs; the invariant test makes M2's byte-identical version strings self-policing; and the ledger's eight explicitly DECLINED ports are the reason my M6 recount landed on the same number it did rather than catching it padding. A candidate that argues against its own score is hard to attack on honesty, and I could not.

attackOnCentralClaim: The claim is: «no claim without evidence» is a compile-time property, not an editorial promise. It survives only in a narrowed form, and the narrowing is larger than the candidate admits. `tsc` enforces exactly one thing — that a value typed `Claim` carries an `evidence` field. It cannot check (i) that the URL resolves, (ii) that the evidence is RELEVANT (a repo-root URL typechecks against any number whatsoever), or (iii) prose written straight into JSX. The candidate concedes (iii) in its own weakestPoint and does not concede (i) or (ii) — and (ii) is where it breaks concretely. Its stated rationale for root-only linking is that «GitHub renders README.md at the repo root, which is where every status and number on the page actually comes from». I grepped climx/README.md for all six numbers it plans to print — 66.66, 98.92, 51/51, 44,266, 463 B, 9,852 — and got 0 hits. Every one lives three directories down in docs/planning/MEASUREMENTS.md. Worse, the README a clicking reader DOES land on says «41 tests» while the page says 51/51, so the design's own one-click destination contradicts its own page. The candidate flagged the 41/50/51 inconsistency in contentGaps and flagged the root-only rule in evidenceModel, and never noticed they collide. Second breakage: the Vitest «invariant» is presented as mechanical enforcement, but the five READMEs live outside the portfolio repo at F:\\Phyriad\\projects\\*, so the test can only assert content.ts's '0.1.0-experimental' equals a literal in the test file — a change-detector, not a truth-checker, blind to README drift. Third: M-3 says «ProjectCard rewritten as a whole-card Link using the ported EstadoCard .link CSS» while the home spec puts «el cluster de evidencia (repositorio · sitio en vivo)» inside that same card — an `<a>` inside an `<a>`. Invalid HTML that jsx-a11y recommended will not catch, and dropping the cluster to fix it falsifies the candidate's own sentence that on `/` all three assertions are one click from the README. THE COMPETITOR IS REAL, NOT A STRAWMAN. The named workload has the reader ARRIVING from a GitHub profile, and for the 20-second screen a well-written profile README genuinely wins: it renders in the reader's existing context with zero navigation, deep-links to any file (which this design forbids itself), needs no separate deploy, and renders images just as well. WHERE THIS DESIGN WINS: the reader who stays. Per-project routes with each project's self-declared limits quoted, a non-uniform status grid, and figures at controlled size are things a README does badly, and M2 = 5/5 verified across five READMEs is a real result no profile README achieves by accident. WHERE IT EMBARRASSES ITSELF: the non-Spanish-reading recruiter O1 names, meeting a Spanish `/` served by ~3 of 16 files, whose evidence cluster is the one element the card rewrite cannot render — while 13 files and an entire /colofon route sit behind a click that reader will never make.

smugglingCheck: Clean, and unusually so — I looked for it specifically. The FORBIDDEN climx `public/img/estados/*.webp` state photographs appear nowhere: the design ports EstadoCard's MECHANISM only (the `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}img/...` helper and the `onError` degrade), which the objective's FORBIDDEN clause explicitly names as «NOT forbidden and encouraged, pointed at the operator's own images», and it drops the `<li>/Link` wrapper, the whole estado/ides domain, and the `.img` rule that displayed the photos. The two images it does use are the operator's own work product, verified on disk. No DROPPED driver reappears under a new name either: no fetchWithCache, no useFetch, no staleness layer, no geo layer, no SearchCombobox, no AgeBanner/ForecastCard/skyIcon/NearestMunicipio/CommonsGallery — and /colofon's «Qué dejé fuera a propósito» section names the data layer, the geo layer, the ARIA combobox, the weather components and the state photos as deliberate refusals, i.e. it converts the smuggling check into page content. The one thing worth naming that is NOT smuggling: PrimitivesLab is a high-value inventory entry, not a dropped driver, so porting it as a colophon section is admissible — and the candidate declines to count it toward M6 anyway.
optimalityHonesty: No unscoped absolute claim anywhere. Every superlative I found carries an explicit referent: «the single thing climx's router does that a hand-rolled switch would not» (a mechanical claim about :param matching, which I verified is true), «an improvement on the donor» (scoped to the named donor and argued), «the highest-value CONTENT in the donor», «the single strongest thing this design takes from climx», «the strongest presentation number available for the climx card», «the weakest possible reading of M6». It never claims to be the best candidate or an optimal design. It goes further than required in the other direction: weakestPoint concedes that a sibling candidate («D3») would have built the served route with 3 files instead of 16, and metricSelfEstimates for M6 pre-concedes a hedged entry and states the fallback score (4) if a recount rejects it — which mine did. defects.finding: The 'repo-ROOT links only' rule breaks the evidence chain on the one project it matters most for, and its stated justification is factually false. Grep of F:\Phyriad\projects\climx\README.md for the six MEASUREMENTS numbers the page will print (66.66 / 98.92 / 51/51 / 44,266 / 463 B / 9,852) returns 0 hits — all six live in docs/planning/MEASUREMENTS.md, three levels down. So 0 of 6 climx doc-claims are one click from a page containing the number, against the design's assertion that «GitHub renders README.md at the repo root, which is where every status and number on the page actually comes from». Worse, the README the reader lands on says «41 tests» while the page says «51/51» — a visible contradiction one click from the claim, which is quality-veto territory. The candidate flagged the 41/50/51 inconsistency and the root-only rule separately and never connected them.

The home card is not implementable as specified. M-3 says «ProjectCard rewritten as a whole-card Link using the ported EstadoCard .link CSS»; the `/` section spec puts «el cluster de evidencia (repositorio · sitio en vivo cuando existe)» inside that same card. That is an `<a>` nested inside an `<a>` — invalid HTML and a keyboard-navigation hazard. Verified that eslint.config.js loads only jsxA11y.configs.recommended, which has no nested-interactive rule, so M4/M5(a) go green over it. Resolving it the other way (drop the cluster from `/`) directly falsifies the candidate's own sentence: «On `/` each project carries exactly three assertions ... plus one evidence cluster, so all three are one click from the README that states them» — the very M1 claim for the highest-priority route in the named workload.

«M1 becomes a compile-time property, not an editorial habit» is overstated by roughly the amount that matters. `tsc` enforces the PRESENCE of an `evidence` field on `Claim`-typed values and nothing else: it cannot check link liveness, and it cannot check evidence RELEVANCE — `{text:'1,409 LUT4 of 6,864', evidence:{kind:'repo', url:<root>}}` typechecks perfectly, which is exactly the pattern the design mandates. The candidate concedes only the third hole (JSX prose). /colofon is six sections of almost entirely free prose, so the design's own thesis route is the route least covered by the design's own mechanism.

The Vitest content invariant is sold as the second mechanical enforcement of M1/M2 but cannot verify anything external. The five READMEs live outside the portfolio repo (F:\Phyriad\projects\<name>\README.md); the test can only assert that content.ts's '0.1.0-experimental' equals a string literal written in the test file. That is a change-detector, not a truth-checker: it is structurally incapable of catching README drift, which is precisely the M2 failure mode it is presented as guarding.

/colofon is scope spent at zero metric return under the frozen metric set. It cannot raise M1 (it adds un-Claim-typed prose, so it can only lower it), it cannot raise M6 (the candidate itself declines both of its ports — PrimitivesShowcase and the ARCHITECTURE weakest-point stance — as non-structural), and it adds ~2-3 KB gzip to M3. It consumes roughly 3 of the 16 files on the axis the objective made a hard disqualifier, on a design whose own weakestPoint concedes `/` is served by ~3 of 16 files. Its claim «construida con los recursos de climx» is also the one claim on the page whose proof is not one click: verifying the reuse ledger requires diffing two repos.

M3(b) is priced at ~240 KB assuming compressed transport. Recomputed uncompressed against my own numbers — 222,600 B JS raw + ~5,100 B CSS + 167,722 B PNG + 750 B HTML = ~396 KB — headroom under the 500 KB cap falls from 52% to 21%. It still fits, so this is bounded, but the objective names `npm run preview` rather than the deployed host as the M3(b) instrument and the candidate never prices that case.

M5(b) is self-scored clean while inheriting a real wart verbatim. climx's app.tsx is `<div className="page" id="contenido">` with no `tabindex="-1"` (read first-hand), so the adopted skip link points at a non-focusable element and will not reliably move focus. M5(b) requires every interactive element to be keyboard-operable; this is the one place the ported shell does not deliver and the candidate books no cost for it.

E8's 16-file budget omits any CSS module for ProjectPage (breadcrumb + «Límites declarados») and for ColophonPage's «Números medidos» table. Worst case is 18 of 18 — the K7 bound exactly, zero margin. (Two mitigations verified in the candidate's favour: climx's PrimitivesLab carries no module CSS, and portfolio's ProjectCard.module.css already exists so the EstadoCard port is a rewrite.)

E7's signature rule («every code file ends with `Made with my soul - Swately <3`») is never mentioned across the 16-file plan. The ported climx files carry it already; the nine net-new authored files are unbudgeted for it. Trivially cheap to satisfy, but an envelope constraint the design never acknowledges.

M6 clears K2 (floor 3) by 1 but clears the ≥4 TARGET by exactly 0 on my recount, and one of the four is manufactured. NotFound.tsx counts as structural only because the ported router's own prop type is `{routes: Route[]; fallback: ComponentType}` with `fallback` non-optional (verified) — i.e. resource #1 creates resource #3's structurality, and any 5-line component satisfies the slot. A strict distinct-capability reading gives 3, which passes K2 and misses M6's target.

Two small self-report inaccuracies, both in the conservative direction and neither load-bearing: climx/router.test.tsx has 10 `it(` blocks against a portfolio baseline of 6, so M-1 lands at 16 tests, not «about 15»; and the two tsconfigs do not «differ only in comments» — `diff` returns exit 0 with empty output, they are byte-identical.

salvageables: Rendering each project's status as the literal README version string PLUS that README's own qualifier sentence. I diffed all five and this is the strongest thing in the candidate: Phynned's «provisional y en revalidación» reproduces README line 232's 'provisional and under re-validation'; Phyriager's «el mod compila pero no se ha validado en vivo en un servidor' reproduces its README exactly; PHarvard carries the 2026-08-01 date from its own State table. This produces a verified 5/5 on the objective's top-priority metric and is portable to any page structure.

The `Evidence` discriminated union as a SHAPE — repo / live / doc / figure, with `doc` carrying value + file path + repo URL together. The compile-time guarantee it is wrapped in is oversold, but the four-kind taxonomy correctly distinguishes the kinds of proof this operator's projects actually have.

The declared two-figures-of-five asymmetry: using only phyriadfg_multigpu.png and trazado_1.png, leaving the other three project routes visibly figure-less, and refusing to fabricate the missing climx/Phynned/PHarvard screenshots — with the layout made to read as deliberate rather than unfinished.

Excluding climx's Lighthouse numbers because MEASUREMENTS.md records them against https://swately.github.io/project-tw/, the pre-rename URL, and E5 has no Lighthouse to re-run them with. I verified both facts; this is the single cleanest piece of evidential discipline in the candidate and it costs it its best presentation number.

The refusal ledger: eight to nine genuine climx ports listed and explicitly scored as NOT structural (router tests, the reset.css a11y block, EstadoCard.module.css, PrimitivesLab, the app shell, --color-warning, the README prose, the ARCHITECTURE stance). The objective declares M6 a floor rather than a maximand; this is what not farming P2 looks like in writing.
Counting public/404.html and the main.tsx restore block as ONE resource rather than two. The conservative count is the correct one and it is the kind of arithmetic a recount usually has to force.

The `asset(path)` helper extracted from EstadoCard's `estadoImg` — `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}${path}` — with the onError degrading to a sentence naming the missing file. This is precisely the mechanism the objective's FORBIDDEN clause carves out as encouraged, redirected at the operator's own images, and it has two real consumers on disk today.

Refusing to print an undated «41 tests» for climx given that its README says 41 while MEASUREMENTS.md records 41/41, 50/50 and 51/51 on three different dates — insisting instead on one figure with its date and instrument.

The «Límites declarados» section: each project's page quoting that project's OWN self-stated limits (cannot exceed the display refresh; the empirical catalog is provisional; the mod is not validated live; the point is not speed). This is the objective's «impresses and overstates is worse than plain and holds up» rendered as a page section.

The self-authored weakestPoint that names a sibling candidate as beating this one on the named workload with three files instead of sixteen, and the M6 self-estimate that pre-states its own fallback score if a recount rejects the hedged entry — which mine did.
unverified: I could not verify the six external URLs the entire evidence model rests on — five `github.com/Swately/<repo>` roots plus climx's live URL. I made no network request. The candidate declares this itself as its first contentGap and correctly states that a private repo drops that project's claims to no-link entries and fails the quality veto; it remains an open precondition on both M1 and the veto, and the operator is the only one who can close it.
